q: Benzodiazepines vs barbiturates at the Cl⁻ channel?
a: Benzodiazepines increase the frequency of opening. Barbiturates increase the duration of opening, and at high doses open the channel directly.

q: Why do benzodiazepines have a low ceiling effect?
a: They only help GABA; they don't open the Cl⁻ channel by themselves (no GABA-mimetic action).

q: Where on the GABA-A receptor do benzodiazepines bind?
a: At the interface of the α and γ subunits. GABA binds the β subunit.
